audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL and CL logic: EL topics include EVM opcodes (transient storage EIP-1153), precompiles (BLAKE2 EIP-152), blob gas pricing (EIP-7762), hex utility parsing, ABI interface provision (EIP-7896), and Engine API; CL topics include Deneb light client sync, Fulu P2P data column gossip/custody, EIP-7928 beacon state fork upgrade, and consensus spec fork transitions.

out_of_scope: Execution Layer internals beyond Engine API interface

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions exploiting new opcodes (TSTORE/TLOAD), precompile edge cases (BLAKE2 rounds=MAX_UINT32), or crafted hex inputs causing parsing failures.
Eclipse attacks, send blocks with invalid excess_blob_gas values, or blocks with manipulated blob gas pricing at fork boundaries.
Provide misleading ABI specifications to trick users into approving malicious transactions.

cl_vectors.threat: Propose blocks with invalid data column sidecars, forge KZG proofs, or submit columns to wrong subnets.
Send malicious DataColumnSidecarsByRange/ByRoot responses, withhold data columns for custody groups, resource exhaustion via oversized requests.
Provide crafted light client headers with invalid blob gas fields for pre-Deneb epochs, or headers with incorrect Merkle proofs.
If JWT secret is compromised, send arbitrary forkchoiceUpdated or newPayload calls to manipulate EL canonical chain.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client Data Source via P2P/API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Light client sync protocol (P2P gossip or dedicated API)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers or APIs providing light client headers are unauthenticated. Headers may contain crafted blob gas fields or invalid Merkle proofs targeting pre-Deneb/Capella epoch boundaries.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block header propagation (P2P network, excess_blob_gas field)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers are untrusted peers. They could craft blocks with incorrect excess_blob_gas values, particularly at the EIP-7762 fork boundary where the reset logic applies.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract/EOA Calling BLAKE2 F Precompile
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL to address 0x09 with 213-byte input
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract or transaction can call the BLAKE2 precompile. Input is fully attacker-controlled: rounds parameter, state vector, message block, and final flag must all be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API (from CL perspective)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API responses (newPayload results, getPayload responses)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The EL communicates with CL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. Authentication channel is trusted, but EL response content (e.g., block_access_list_root in EIP-7928) must still be validated by CL.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API (from EL perspective)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (forkchoiceUpdated, newPayload, getPayload on port 8551)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL is authenticated via JWT shared secret. However, payload content (execution payloads, forkchoice state) must be validated by EL. An attacker with compromised JWT could send arbitrary API calls.

trusted_external_entities.name: Any Entity Connecting to Engine API Port
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Before JWT authentication succeeds, any connecting entity is untrusted. JWT authentication gates access, but the port itself is exposed. Failed auth attempts must be handled gracefully.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via wallet_sendCalls Interface
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps provide ABI specifications that wallets use to decode calldata for user display. A malicious DApp can provide fake ABIs that misrepresent the actual function being called, misleading users into approving harmful transactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious DApp Providing Fake ABI
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: wallet_sendCalls RPC with misleading interface specifications
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker-controlled application providing ABIs that misrepresent transaction function calls. This is an explicit attack vector in EIP-7896's security model.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User Approving Transactions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: End users may approve transactions based on misleading decoded calldata. Users are external actors whose approval decisions drive transaction signing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Trusted ABI Database (4byte.directory, Sourcify, Etherscan)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Wallets may validate DApp-provided ABIs against external databases. These databases are semi-trusted: they operate over authenticated channels (HTTPS) but their content completeness and accuracy cannot be fully guaranteed.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Gossip Peer Broadcasting Data Columns
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. They can broadcast data column sidecars with invalid KZG proofs, incorrect subnet routing, forged proposer signatures, or tampered inclusion proofs.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Requesting Data Columns via Req/Resp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Requesting peers are unauthenticated. They may send requests with excessively large ranges, invalid block roots, or column indices outside bounds to cause resource exhaustion.

trusted_external_entities.name: External Hex String Input Source via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC parameters, configuration files, and test data containing hex strings
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Hex input can come from any unauthenticated source. Malformed hex strings (invalid characters, extreme lengths) could cause parsing exceptions or memory exhaustion if not properly validated.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All light client headers must pass: (1) blob gas field validation for pre-Deneb epochs (must be zero), (2) execution payload emptiness check for pre-Capella epochs, (3) Merkle branch verification of execution root against beacon body root. Headers from any source are fully untrusted.

Block header excess_blob_gas must exactly match calc_excess_blob_gas computation with timestamp-based fork boundary reset. Mismatch must result in block rejection. Special attention needed at fork boundary where excess_blob_gas resets to 0.

Input must be exactly 213 bytes. Final flag byte must be exactly 0 or 1. Gas cost = rounds * 1 must be available. High rounds values (up to 2^32-1) are valid but gas-metered. All input fields (h, m, t, f) are attacker-controlled and must produce deterministic RFC 7693 output.

The block_access_list_root provided by EL must be validated by CL. At fork transition it is initialized to Root() (zero). Post-fork, CL must verify EL-provided values are consistent with execution payload content.

JWT authentication required. ForkchoiceState must be validated: headBlockHash must reference a known valid payload, safeBlockHash must be ancestor of head, finalizedBlockHash must be consistent. Payload attributes must have valid timestamp. Message ordering must be enforced sequentially.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API JWT authentication on port 8551
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All requests must present a valid JWT bearer token signed with the shared secret. Invalid or missing JWT must result in immediate rejection. The shared secret must be securely generated and stored. Communication should occur over localhost or trusted network.

DApp-provided ABIs are untrusted. Wallets must: (1) validate interface spec version, (2) perform case-sensitive address matching, (3) optionally verify against trusted ABI database, (4) clearly indicate to users when ABI source is unverified. Decoded calldata display must not be presented as authoritative.

Wallets must assume all DApp-provided ABIs could be misleading. Users must be warned that decoded transaction details are only as trustworthy as the providing DApp. Wallets should indicate verified vs. unverified ABI sources visually.

User approval drives transaction signing. Wallet must present accurate information about trust level of decoded data. Users may be misled by malicious ABIs; wallet UI must distinguish verified from unverified decoded calldata.

Database responses are delivered over HTTPS. Database may not have entries for all contracts. Absence of verification does not imply malicious intent. Wallet must handle missing entries gracefully and indicate unverified status to user.

Full validation pipeline required: (1) correct subnet routing (column_index % SUBNET_COUNT == subnet_id), (2) temporal bounds (not future, within finalized range), (3) proposer signature verification, (4) KZG commitments inclusion Merkle proof, (5) batch KZG proof verification, (6) proposer index matches expected shuffling. REJECT for cryptographic failures, IGNORE for timing issues.

Request parameters must be validated: start_slot and count within data_column_serve_range, request size within MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB limits, block_root since minimum_request_epoch. Oversized requests must be rejected. Resource unavailability (code 3) returned for data outside serve range.

Input must contain only valid hex characters (0-9, a-f, A-F) after optional 0x prefix. Fixed-size outputs enforce exact byte lengths via padding. Type wrappers (U8, U64, U256) must enforce bounds checking. Invalid input must raise handled exceptions, not crash the node.
